title: Onramp: usage lab and gradual migration playbook for tokens, buttons, tables, charts
creator: Priya Desai
description: Background: The tokens, buttons, tables and charts families have accumulated divergent examples and partial migration notes across the docsite. Engineers onboarding to Redwood often misuse token scales or mix legacy props with new primitives which creates layout regressions and visual debt. Goal: ship an 'Onramp Usage Lab' — an opinionated, interactive documentation section that clarifies recommended usage patterns, clear do/don't examples, API reference snippets, and a gradual migration playbook for teams moving from legacy tokens/components to the consolidated primitives. Scope: - Usage heuristics and clear 'when to use' guidance for tokens (semantic vs raw scales) - Button variants: primary/secondary/ghost with accessibility rules and dos/don'ts - Table patterns: density, column resizing, row actions, performance tips for large datasets - Charts: recommended data-to-visual mappings, color token usage, and accessibility considerations Deliverables: 1) A new docsite page "Onramp Usage Lab" with interactive sandboxes for 4 families (tokens, buttons, tables, charts). 2) Migration playbook with checklist by component family and ready-to-copy code snippets. 3) Updated component API docs that consolidate legacy prop deprecations and recommended patterns. 4) One internal demo session + slide deck for Eng/PM to adopt the playbook.
acceptance_criteria: Onramp Usage Lab page merged to docsite branch and renders in staging
Interactive sandboxes for each family include at least two working examples and a 'broken example' with explanation
Migration playbook includes step-by-step checklist and backstop strategies (feature flags, visual regression guardrails)
Component API pages updated to include clear deprecation table and canonical examples
Documentation reviewed and signed off by Design, Platform Engineering, and Docs owner
